column2: What are MPs’ local meetings with constituents called?
Surgeries
Clinics
Hearings
Assemblies
Often advertised in the local newspaper.
The PM also has a country house called Chequers.
What is the name of the Prime Minister’s country house?
Balmoral
Sandringham
Outside London.
Which minister is responsible for crime, policing and immigration?
The Chancellor
The Justice Secretary
The Foreign Secretary manages relationships with foreign countries.
Which party is the opposition?
The second-largest party in the House of Commons
All parties not in government
The largest party in the House of Lords
The party that came third
Its leader usually becomes PM if it wins the next election.
What do the senior opposition MPs appointed by the leader of the opposition form?
The shadow cabinet
The Speaker’s committee
They challenge the government and put forward alternatives.
How often does Prime Minister’s Questions take place whilst Parliament is sitting?
Every week
Every day
Every month
Once a year
An opportunity for the opposition to point out failures.
Greenpeace and Liberty
Which TWO are core values of the civil service?
Impartiality
Loyalty to the governing party
Integrity
Secrecy
Integrity, honesty, objectivity and impartiality (including political neutrality).
Impartiality and Integrity
Is the statement below true or false? "Civil servants are political appointees."
They are chosen on merit and are politically neutral.
Civil servants are political appointees.
Coordinated by the Greater London Authority and the Mayor of London.
When are local elections for councillors held in most areas?
In May every year
Every five years in June
In September
At the same time as General Elections
Many candidates stand as members of a political party.
Also immigration, taxation and social security.
Defence and Foreign affairs
How many members does the Scottish Parliament have?
Elected by a form of proportional representation.
How many members does the Welsh Assembly have?
Elections every four years using proportional representation.
How many members does the Northern Ireland Assembly have?
With a power-sharing agreement among the main parties.
Since when has the Welsh Assembly been able to pass laws in its areas without the UK Parliament’s agreement?
In 20 areas, including education, health, economic development and housing.
Shortly after the Troubles broke out in {#}.
What are the official reports of proceedings in Parliament called?
The Gazette
The Record
The Times
Available in large libraries and at www.parliament.uk.
Is the statement below true or false? "By law, radio and television coverage of political parties must be balanced."
Equal time must be given to rival viewpoints.
By law, radio and television coverage of political parties must be balanced.
Who can stand for election as an MP?
Anyone aged {#} or over (with some exceptions)
Only party members over {#}
Only people born in the UK
Only members of the House of Lords
But they are unlikely to win without a major party.
Since which year has the UK had a fully democratic voting system?
The voting age of {#} was set in {#}.
Which TWO groups resident in the UK can vote in all public elections?
Commonwealth citizens
Citizens of other EU states
Irish citizens
Tourists
Along with UK citizens. EU citizens can vote in all elections except General Elections.
Commonwealth citizens and Irish citizens
Is the statement below true or false? "Citizens of other EU states resident in the UK can vote in General Elections."
They can vote in all elections except General Elections.
Citizens of other EU states resident in the UK can vote in General Elections.
When is the electoral register updated?
Every year in September or October
Every January
Before each election only
A form is sent to every household.
What are polling stations called in Scotland?
Polling places
Voting booths
Ballot halls
Polling stations
Polling places.
What are the opening hours of polling stations on election day?
{#}.{#} am to midnight
Your poll card tells you where and when to vote.
If it is difficult to get to a polling station, what can you do?
Register for a postal ballot
Vote by phone
Ask a neighbour to vote
Vote at the town hall a week later
Your ballot paper is sent to your home.
Which TWO groups cannot stand for public office?
Members of the armed forces
Teachers
Civil servants
Doctors
Also people found guilty of certain criminal offences.
Members of the armed forces and Civil servants
Is the statement below true or false? "Members of the House of Lords may stand for election to the House of Commons."
They may not, but are eligible for all other public offices.
Members of the House of Lords may stand for election to the House of Commons.
Where do members of the Scottish Parliament meet?
MLAs meet at Stormont; AMs at the Senedd.
Where does the Northern Ireland Assembly meet?
Hillsborough Castle
Visits can be arranged through the Education Service or an MLA.
Who is the ceremonial head of the Commonwealth?
The UN Secretary-General
The Commonwealth Secretary
Currently King Charles III.
Which TWO are core values of the Commonwealth?
A single currency
A shared army
Democracy, good government and the rule of law.
It has no power over its members, although it can suspend membership. Membership is voluntary.
The Commonwealth has power over its members.
Which TWO countries were founder members of the EEC in {#}?
Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.
France and Luxembourg
Signed by six western European countries.
How many member states does the EU now have?
After the UK left in {#}.
It has no power to make laws but draws up conventions and charters.
Is the statement below true or false? "The Council of Europe is part of the EU."
It is separate from the EU and has 47 member countries, including the UK.
The Council of Europe is part of the EU.
How many members are there on the UN Security Council?
The UK is one of five permanent members.
When was the United Nations set up?
After the Second World War
After the First World War
In {#}
To prevent war and promote international peace and security.
What is NATO?
European and North American countries that agree to help each other if attacked
A trade agreement
A human rights court
A Commonwealth committee
It also aims to keep peace between its members.
What are European laws called?
Directives, regulations or framework decisions
Acts and bills
Statutes
Conventions only
From {#}, no general principle of EU law is part of UK law.
Which Act incorporated the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law?
The Human Rights Act {#}
The Bill of Rights {#}
The Equality Act {#}
The Magna Carta
The government, public bodies and the courts must follow it.
Right to a fair trial and Prohibition of torture
A man who forces his wife to have sex can be charged with rape.
Arranged marriages where both people agree are acceptable. Forced marriage is a criminal offence.
Arranged marriages are illegal in the UK.
What is the maximum jail term for breaching a Forced Marriage Protection Order?
Up to two years
Up to six months
Up to ten years
Life
For contempt of court.
Is the statement below true or false? "Taking a girl abroad for female genital mutilation (FGM) is a criminal offence."
FGM is illegal in the UK.
Also age, sex, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and sexuality.
Disability and Marital status
Which TWO are paid for by income tax?
Roads
Your private pension
Your mortgage
Also education and the armed forces.
Roads and The police
How do self-employed people pay tax?
Through self-assessment, including a tax return
Through PAYE
They do not pay tax
Through their bank automatically
They also pay their own National Insurance Contributions.
Which TWO are paid for by National Insurance Contributions?
The state retirement pension
The armed forces
The NHS
NI pays for state benefits and services.
The state retirement pension and The NHS
When are young people sent a National Insurance number?
Just before their {#}th birthday
At birth
At {#}
When they start work
A unique personal account number.
Is the statement below true or false? "You can start work without a National Insurance number."
But you will need one. Contact the DWP.
You can start work without a National Insurance number.
There are other requirements for large vehicles.
In Northern Ireland, what must a newly qualified driver display for one year?
An R plate (restricted driver)
An L plate
A P plate
An N plate
R stands for restricted driver.
When must a vehicle take an MOT test every year?
When it is over three years old
When it is over one year old
Every year from new
When it is over ten years old
It is an offence not to have an MOT certificate.
Where must vehicles be registered?
The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA)
HMRC
The local police
You must also pay annual road tax and have insurance.
Is the statement below true or false? "It is a serious criminal offence to drive without insurance."
You must have valid motor insurance.
Which TWO parts make up the driving theory test?
A multiple choice test
A practical road test
A hazard perception test
An eyesight test
You then need to pass a practical driving test.
A multiple choice test and A hazard perception test
Carrying a weapon and Selling tobacco to under-{#}s
Which TWO are examples of civil law?
Consumer rights disputes about faulty goods
Racial crime
Debt
Buying drugs
Also housing law and employment law.
Consumer rights disputes about faulty goods and Debt
It is legal to carry a knife for self-defence.
At what age can you legally be sold tobacco products?
It is illegal to sell tobacco to anyone under {#}.
Which TWO are duties of the police?
Protecting life and property
Making laws
Preventing and detecting crime
